name_en: Aburaage — thin sheets of tofu deep-fried until they puff hollow
summary_ja: 薄く切った豆腐を低温と高温の油で二度揚げし、中が空洞になるまで膨らませた大豆の加工品。関西では薄揚げ、北陸や東北ではあぶらげとも呼ばれ、きつねうどんやいなり寿司、味噌汁や煮物に広く使われるとされる。
summary_en: Thin slices of tofu fried twice, first in cooler oil and then in hot, until they puff up and hollow out. Called usuage in Kansai and aburage in Hokuriku and Tohoku, it is said to be the workhorse behind kitsune udon, inari sushi, miso soup and simmered dishes alike.

name_en: Atsuage — thick-cut tofu fried only on the outside, still soft within
summary_ja: 厚く切った豆腐を高温の油で揚げ、表面だけを香ばしく固めて中は豆腐のまま残した加工品。油揚げと違って中が生に近いことから生揚げとも呼ばれ、煮物や焼き物、おでんの種として広く使われるとされる。
summary_en: Thick slabs of tofu fried in hot oil so that only the surface browns and firms while the inside stays soft tofu. Because the center remains nearly raw it is also called nama-age, and it is said to be a staple for simmering, grilling and oden.

name_en: Tochio aburaage — Niigata's oversized, skewer-drained fried tofu
summary_ja: 新潟県長岡市栃尾地区で作られる、手のひらほどの大判で厚みのある油揚げ。低温と高温で二度揚げしたのち金串に刺して立て、油を切るのが昔ながらの仕事とされ、焼いてねぎと醤油で食べると外は香ばしく中はふっくらしているという。
summary_en: A palm-sized, unusually thick aburaage from the Tochio district of Nagaoka, Niigata. Fried twice and then speared on metal skewers to stand and drain, the traditional way, it is said to grill up crisp outside and fluffy within, eaten with green onion and soy sauce.

name_en: Nankan-age — Kumamoto's paper-dry, long-keeping fried tofu sheets
summary_ja: 熊本県南関町に伝わる、水分をしっかり抜いて揚げた大判で薄い油揚げ。乾いてパリパリとしているため常温で長く保存でき、煮物や味噌汁に入れると煮汁を吸ってふっくらと戻るとされる。海苔の代わりに巻き寿司の皮にも使われるという。
summary_en: A large, thin aburaage from Nankan, Kumamoto, made from tofu pressed nearly dry before frying. Crisp and dry enough to keep at room temperature for weeks, it is said to swell back to softness in simmering liquid or miso soup, and is even used in place of nori to wrap sushi rolls.
source_title: 南関あげ巻き寿司（熊本県）

name_ja: 高野豆腐（凍み豆腐・凍り豆腐）
name_en: Koya-dofu — tofu frozen, aged and dried into a sponge that drinks up dashi
summary_ja: 固めの豆腐を凍らせ、低温で寝かせてから解凍・脱水し乾燥させた保存食。高野山の精進料理に由来する高野豆腐の名のほか、信州や東北では寒風に吊るす凍み豆腐、凍り豆腐とも呼ばれ、戻して煮含めるとスポンジ状の生地がだしを抱えるとされる。
summary_en: A preserved food made by freezing firm tofu, holding it cold, then thawing, pressing and drying it. Known as koya-dofu after the temple cooking of Mount Koya, and as shimi-dofu or kori-dofu in Shinshu and Tohoku where blocks were hung in the winter wind, it rehydrates into a sponge that holds dashi in every pore.

name_en: Yuba — the delicate skin lifted from gently heated soy milk
summary_ja: 豆乳を静かに温めたとき表面に張る薄い膜をすくい上げた大豆の加工品。京都では湯葉、日光では湯波と書き、生のままわさび醤油で食べるほか、乾かして煮物や吸い物に使うとされる。寺院の精進料理とともに広まったと伝わる。
summary_en: The thin skin that forms on soy milk as it is warmed gently, lifted off and eaten as is. Written 湯葉 in Kyoto and 湯波 in Nikko, it is eaten fresh with wasabi and soy sauce or dried for simmered dishes and clear soups, and is said to have spread with temple vegetarian cooking.

name_en: Nikko yuba — the thick, double-folded soy-milk skin of Nikko's temple town
summary_ja: 栃木県日光市で作られる湯波。京都の湯葉が一枚ずつ薄く引くのに対し、日光では膜を二つ折りにして引き上げる二枚引きで厚みを出すとされ、「波」の字を当てる。生のほか、巻いて干した巻き湯波や揚げた揚げ巻き湯波が煮物に使われるという。
summary_en: Yuba from Nikko, Tochigi, written with the character for 'wave'. Where Kyoto lifts each skin as a single thin sheet, Nikko is said to fold the skin double as it is raised, giving it body. Beyond fresh yuba, rolled dried maki-yuba and fried agemaki-yuba go into the town's simmered dishes.
source_title: 揚げまき湯波の煮物（栃木県）

name_en: Kyo-yuba — Kyoto's thin, single-lift yuba from the temple-gate workshops
summary_ja: 京都で作られる湯葉。膜を一枚ずつ薄く引き上げる一枚引きが基本とされ、引き上げてすぐの生湯葉、膜が張る前の豆乳をすくう汲み上げ湯葉、乾かした干し湯葉などに作り分けられるという。禅寺の精進料理と軟水に支えられて門前に湯葉屋が育ったと伝わる。
summary_en: Yuba as made in Kyoto, where the skin is lifted one thin layer at a time. Makers are said to divide it into fresh yuba lifted and served at once, kumiage-yuba scooped from the milk before a skin fully forms, and dried sheets, a craft said to have grown at the temple gates on Zen vegetarian cooking and soft water.

name_en: Hoshi-yuba — dried yuba sheets and rolls kept for soups and simmering
summary_ja: 引き上げた湯葉を乾かして保存できるようにした乾物。平らな平湯葉、細く巻いた巻き湯葉、小さく結んだものなど形はさまざまで、ぬるま湯で戻して吸い物や煮物に使うとされる。生では日持ちしない膜を蓄える知恵として寺院の台所から広まったと伝わる。
summary_en: Yuba dried so that it keeps: flat sheets, slender rolls, little knots and more. Rehydrated in warm water, it goes into clear soups and simmered dishes. It is said to have spread from temple kitchens as a way to store a skin that would not last fresh.
source_title: 揚げまき湯波の煮物（栃木県）
